source.title: Neural scaling laws for deep regression on domain image data of twisted magnets

record.tranche_reason: The study tests scaling relationships in image-based deep regression and reports that power-law behavior depends on the target, model and training setup, with breakdowns in some data and model-size regimes. This refines the scope of scaling-law claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own scaling measurements for deep regression on magnetic-domain images. It does not test language-model cross-entropy or compute-optimal allocations. Results it cites from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own scaling sweeps (dataset size and FCN model size) for MSE test loss of image-input deep regression models. This is a new setting outside text pretraining, so it bears on V5. Its results on how exponents shift with target, architecture, depth, learning-rate schedule and activation bear on V7's setup-dependence, though in a regression setting, not language models. T3 fits better than T5: the paper mainly reports that power laws hold in a new setting, with regime limits.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that deep-regression test loss shows power-law scaling with dataset size, and (for J and D) model size, across FCN, ResNet-18 and ViT. Exponents are large (about 1 to 2.3), well above typical classification or language values. The exponents depend on the regressed parameter and model details. They note breakdowns at large datasets and no model-size power law for θ, and call for case-by-case analysis. They also present the large exponents as implying substantial gains from more data.
record.recipe_differences: This is an empirical study of MSE test loss for image-input deep regression on simulated magnetic-domain data, varying dataset and model size. It does not use language-model next-token cross-entropy, language-model training runs, or compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior varies with regression target, model size, architecture and depth, learning-rate schedule, activation function, dataset size, and numerical-precision limits.
record.problems: Results concern one simulated magnetic-domain regression task, not language models or held-out cross-entropy. Several plotted comparisons lack numerical values in the text. The authors report numerical-precision limits, stochastic variation, and departures from power-law behavior in some regimes; the large-dataset exponents for some targets are less definitive.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results left out.

untested.parts: Video or other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer; compute scaling; generative or self-supervised training regimes.
Language-model exponents; compute-optimal split; parameter-counting conventions; fitting-method comparisons across published laws.
Extrapolation from small to much larger runs; not tested.

missing.what: Arithmetic mean and median of test loss give exponents in quantitative agreement with the geometric mean. This is a fitting/aggregation choice that does not change the exponents.
L2 regularization and dropout did not improve the consistency of the scaling behaviour (details in Supplementary Information).
Fixed learning rate gives consistent power-law scaling for small models up to the largest dataset; the fluctuations occur only for large models.
Exponents for θ and D decline at the largest dataset sizes, which the authors attribute to dependence on the training scheme.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The setting is image-input regression on simulated magnetic-domain data with MSE loss, not language-model cross-entropy. V7 links therefore show setup-dependence of exponents in this domain only, not for published LM laws. ResNet-18 and ViT each use a single model size. The precision floor of about 1.9e-7 confounds the large-dataset behaviour for θ and D.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy and its scaling with parameters, tokens or compute.
Whether fits on small runs predict the losses of runs orders of magnitude larger.
Compute-budget sweeps and the loss-minimising allocation between parameters and tokens.
The study compares architectures but does not report a controlled comparison at a fixed parameter count establishing that depth, width and other architecture details change loss only slightly.
Tests image-input deep regression on simulated magnetic-domain data, not other modalities such as video, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer.
Downstream-task performance and its predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
Does not compare language-model exponents or compute-optimal splits across parameter-counting, data, or fitting choices; no compute-optimal split is measured.
